stories.event: Israelis voted on Tuesday 27 October 2026 for the 120-seat Knesset, with turnout near 45% by 14:00, the highest at that hour in 50 years according to the Central Elections Committee (CEC). Final polls on 23 October gave Netanyahu's bloc (Likud with New Hope, Shas, United Torah Judaism, Religious Zionist Party–Zehut, Otzma Yehudit) roughly 48–53 seats and left both it and the Eisenkot-led opposition short of the 61-seat majority. In 2022 the bloc beat its polls by about four seats and won 64. The CEC counts regular ballots overnight and double-envelope ballots (soldiers, diplomats and others) from 28 October; in 2022 the count was 99% complete two days after the vote. The question is whether the CEC count as it stands at the end of Thursday 29 October gives Netanyahu's camp a majority.

stories.event: A local ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region, brokered with the involvement of US First Lady Melania Trump, took effect at 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October 2026 and is due to run until 1 November. Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said no violations had been recorded by either side as of 17:30 on 27 October. The notice of 27 October set diesel at CZK 49.46/l for 28–29 October (+0.50, the October high, after +0.27 a day earlier), while petrol eased to 44.45. stories.event: The Académie française awards its Grand prix du roman 2026 on Thursday 29 October by secret ballot of the academicians. Its final shortlist has three novels: Yannick Haenel's 'La solitude des professeurs est infinie' (Gallimard), Sébastien Lapaque's 'Le Rappel des oiseaux' (Actes Sud) and Marie Petitcuénot's 'Heures sauvages' (Héloïse d'Ormesson). On 27 October the Académie Goncourt named its final four for the 3 November Goncourt: Haenel, Philippe Jaenada, Clémentine Mélois and Sylvain Prudhomme, so Haenel is the only author on both lists. The 2025 Grand prix du roman went to Yanick Lahens.

stories.event: On 27 October Culture Minister Oto Klempíř (Motoristé) removed former ČT director-general Petr Dvořák as chair of the State Audiovisual Fund board. The reasons he gave were differing views on the fund's management and a lack of cooperation on savings. The 15-member board had unanimously refused his request to cut planned 2027 support by about CZK 400m (51%) and kept CZK 787.5m. Fourteen film-industry organisations led by APA protested, and ex-minister Baxa called it a purge. No successor has been named. The cabinet is to approve the fund's 2027 budget on 2 November, and Klempíř plans a law by the end of November to replace the whole board.
